facts.claim: Addon scripts register their options lazily in Script.loadscript(), which the watcher defers, so any code path that dumps/inspects options before scripts load (e.g. --options) will silently miss addon-contributed options unless it explicitly forces pending scripts to load first.
facts.evidence: "Addon scripts register their options in Script.loadscript(), which is deferred by Script.watcher(). When --options is passed, we now load pending scripts before dumping options"

facts.claim: The fix identifies not-yet-loaded script addons via the scriptloader's child addons having `ns is None`, and forces loading by calling `s.loadscript()` on each before the dump — a reusable pattern for forcing deferred addon initialization prior to introspection.

Tests for this kind of deferred-loading bug need both a positive case (an addon script registering a custom option appears in --options output) and a negative control (plain --options without scripts does not spuriously include that option), since a single positive test alone wouldn't prove the fix is addon-specific rather than accidental.
facts.evidence: test_options_includes_addon_options asserts "custom_addon_option" in output; test_options_without_scripts asserts "custom_addon_option" not in output

json.reason: The PR fixes a concrete deferred-initialization bug (scripts register options only on loadscript(), which --options ran before triggering) and introduces a reusable mechanism (iterating scriptloader.addons, checking s.ns is None, calling loadscript()) plus a paired positive/negative test pattern to validate the fix's specificity. These are durable, mechanism-level lessons about addon lifecycle and test design, not styling or narration.
